notes: The project's one pre-declared primary comparison, question written into the huddle notes 2026-08-01 -- before any post-change data existed. 'Successes' is the engine's word for the counted event; here the counted event is a REJECTED order, so both proportions read as defect rates. Groups are pooled window counts (defective orders / orders presented), not daily values, so the floors are the proportion floors: n*phat and n*(1-phat) per sample, both cleared by an order of magnitude (135 and 30 on the small side -- the engine prints the check in the route echo). Routed two_proportion_z; risk difference with Newcombe CI is the effect size. The first two post weeks deliberately EXCLUDE the 2026-08-03 -> 08-08 bedding-in days (the ramp is visible on the monitoring chart) and end before the 08-31 term-start surge, so this comparison is the clean like-for-like one; the proof artifact then covers the full 24-day window with the surge declared as a confounder.

value.effect_size_ci_method: Newcombe (1998) method 10, built from per-sample Wilson score intervals
assumptions_checked: n*phat >= 5 and n*(1-phat) >= 5 per sample cleared (matrix §4a EXIT-06)

plain_language.comparison_summary: Compared the proportion for baseline (2026-06-29 to 2026-07-22) (135/1566 = 8.6%) against post-change weeks 1-2 (2026-08-10 to 2026-08-22) (30/884 = 3.4%) using a two-proportion z-test.
plain_language.p_value_meaning: p = 0.0000, below the alpha=0.05 threshold: if there were truly no difference, a result at least this far from 'no difference' would turn up by chance alone only about 7.1e-05% of the time. That makes the difference statistically detectable here -- it does not mean the null hypothesis is false with that probability, and it says nothing yet about whether the difference is big enough to matter.
plain_language.effect_size_in_words: Risk difference = +5.2% (baseline (2026-06-29 to 2026-07-22) minus post-change weeks 1-2 (2026-08-10 to 2026-08-22)), 95% CI [+3.3%, +7.0%] (Newcombe's method).
plain_language.practical_significance_prompt: Statistically detectable ≠ big enough to matter -- compare the effect size above against the goal.

provenance.method: two-proportion pooled z-test (NIST/SEMATECH §7.3.3, Case 1) + Newcombe (1998) method-10 risk-difference CI
